title: The Cold Lamp

where.detail: a frozen stream running up into the forest from the Wend, a little north of where the company crossed

time: the first morning across the Wend
last_beat: Rae walked the cart up onto the frozen stream into the forest by her grandmother's way, and Darrow came last, with the cold lamp behind them and its black chip turning on its thong in no wind at all.

people.did: Looked back at the five horses on the far bank and the smoke over the reeds; knew the black chip on the lamp-post for the kind of thing he had seen under a lad's tongue; asked Rae which way, and followed.
people.now: Going up a frozen stream into the Thornwild at the back of the company, with Wren.

facts.fact: He put aside the urge to take the obvious line first and asked Rae which way to go.
He saw that the black chip on the lamp-post was like the one taken from under the tongue of the lad in the Grey Cot, scorched.
facts.evidence: He had seen a thing like it once before, no bigger than a barleycorn

people.did: Stopped Wren touching what hung on the lamp; named the wood with her grandmother's word, greth; took the company in by her grandmother's way, up a frozen stream.
people.now: Leading the cart up the frozen stream into the forest, by her grandmother's way.

facts.fact: She told Wren you don't touch what's hung on a lamp, not here.
facts.evidence: "You don't touch what's hung on a lamp," Rae said. "Not here."

facts.fact: Her grandmother's word for the country east of the river is greth, the grey country, and Rae said her gran would not have liked her saying it there.
facts.evidence: "She'd not have liked me saying it here."

facts.fact: Her grandmother came out of the forest by a frozen stream the year she came over, and Rae took the company in by it, knowing it only as her gran had told it.
facts.evidence: "I know the way she told it."

people.did: Noticed there were no bells; reached for the chip on the lamp-post and was stopped.
people.now: Going up the frozen stream at the back with Darrow.

facts.fact: She noticed first that there are no bells in the Thornwild.

people.did: Looked at the black chip on the lamp-post with the face she has for a wound.
people.now: Walking at the cart's tail up the frozen stream.

facts.fact: She looked at the black chip the way she looks at a wound before she touches it.
facts.evidence: her face had the look it got at a wound before she touched it.

people.did: Asked whose door the lamp marked; swore at the stream's angle from the tailboard.
people.now: On the tailboard of Rae's cart going up the frozen stream.

people.did: Stood at the forest's edge with her nose working and her tail going round, then ranged ahead.
people.now: Ranging ahead up the frozen stream.

codex.name: Greth
codex.text: Rae's grandmother's word, said from the belly: the grey country east of the river (Ch 8 Sc 1).

codex.name: The clans' lamps
codex.text: An iron lamp on a post at the edge of the Thornwild, shuttered on three sides and open to the river, with a scorched black chip tied below it on a thong; a lamp at every door, Rae's grandmother said, and a door is anywhere they say it is (Ch 8 Sc 1).

struggle: The forest across the river, and whatever it is full of.

now.against: A forest with no bells, and lamps nobody has lit.
now.next: Up the frozen stream into the Thornwild by Rae's grandmother's way.

title: Bread on a Stump

where.detail: a camp in the lee of the stream bank, within sight of a lit lamp-post, a day up the frozen stream

time: the first full day up the stream, the night, and the next morning
last_beat: In the morning the loaf on the stump was gone, and the red cloth with it; in the snow beside the stump there was one ski-track, coming and going.

people.did: Walked a day beside a watch he could not see; when Ash ate the bread left at a lit lamp, put down the urge to follow the ski-tracks and let Rae say what went down in its place; at dusk the script changed on his palms and he told Wren first.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp, a day up the stream, the script on his hands changed.

facts.fact: He wanted to follow the ski-tracks and apologise to the watch himself, and let Rae set the price instead.
facts.evidence: "It's your gran's word," he said. "You say what goes down."

facts.fact: The word under his name on the script changed, and it sits lower and steadier on his palms, like something tempered.
facts.evidence: The word under his name had changed.

facts.fact: He told Wren first what the script said, before anyone.
facts.evidence: "You're the first. Nobody else has it."

facts.fact: The third finger of his right hand, white after the ring, has come back; the two slow ones have not.
facts.evidence: the third beside them that had come back to him since the ring

people.did: Named tal when Ash ate the bread at the lamp; set down one of the millers' loaves on the red cloth, bread for bread; banked the fire with her three turns.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: Tal, her grandmother's word: a gift laid down at a door before you ask anything of the house, or the asking is an insult.
facts.evidence: "It was a gift laid down before an ask."

facts.fact: She paid back the eaten bread with one of the miller's wife's loaves, bread for bread, same size or bigger, as her grandmother taught her.
facts.evidence: "Bread for bread," she said. "Same size or bigger. That's what she taught me."

facts.fact: She banks the fire with the same three turns of a stick every night and will not say where she learned them.
facts.evidence: Rae banked it with three turns of a stick, the same three as every night

people.did: Offered a pencil for the gift; sat by Darrow at the fire and was told first what the script said; wrote it in two places.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp with the ledger.

facts.fact: When he told her first what the script said, she wrote one under her sum and Five under Told first.
facts.evidence: and wrote *Five.*, and drew a line under it

people.did: Offered a knife and thought better of it; went still at singing in the trees, a tune he half knows, and would not say from where.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: He half knows the tune sung in the trees at night, and would not say from where.
facts.evidence: "No," said Hollis. He put the cup down. "Half of it."

people.did: Would not give her salt, which is for wounds; looked at his foot at the fire, as every night since the mill, and called it pink.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: She would not give her salt as the gift; it is for wounds.
facts.evidence: "Not my salt. That salt's for wounds."

facts.fact: At the fire she looked at his right foot, as every night since the mill, and gave it its first good word: pink.
facts.evidence: "Pink," she said: the first good word she had given it.

people.did: Ate the bread left on the stump at the lit lamp, and brought Darrow the cloth.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: She ate the bread laid down at a clan lamp in front of everyone.
facts.evidence: with the red cloth in her mouth and crumbs in her beard

codex.name: Tal
codex.text: Rae's grandmother's word: a gift laid down at a door before you ask anything of the house; without it the asking is an insult. Bread for bread, same size or bigger (Ch 8 Sc 2).

struggle: A watch he cannot see, and a door he has wronged without knowing it.

now.against: A watch that walks beside them unseen.
